parts.label: a
parts.ask: Relative to \(O\), \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) have position vectors \(12\mathbf{i}\), \(16\mathbf{j}\), \(50\mathbf{i} + 136\mathbf{j}\) and \(22\mathbf{i} + 24\mathbf{j}\). Show that \(AD\) is parallel to \(BC\).
parts.method: Show one vector is a multiple of the other

steps.why: \(B\) is \(16\mathbf{j}\): take it off the \(\mathbf{j}\) part.

parts.answerText: \(\overrightarrow{BC} = 5\overrightarrow{AD}\), a multiple of it, so \(AD\) is parallel to \(BC\).

check.answers: show that: the vectors 10i + 24j and 50i + 120j are multiples (the assert checks 50/10 = 120/24 = 5)

parts.label: b
parts.ask: \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\) are the vertices of a running track (a quadrilateral), with lengths in metres. A runner takes exactly 5 minutes to complete 2 laps. Calculate the runner's average speed in kilometres per hour.
parts.method: Pythagoras for each side, then speed = distance ÷ time

steps.why: Two laps in km, divided by 5 minutes in hours.
